ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached transition-state diagram shows a cyclohexane ring on the left. One ring carbon bears an OH substituent and also a carbon side chain extending to the right. The side chain connects to a nitrogen, which is double-bonded to a second nitrogen; that second nitrogen is connected to an OH2 group. Curved arrows and charge marks are present but are to be disregarded for bond counting. Reasoning: Excluding all bonds to hydrogen, count the heavy-atom bonds region by region. The cyclohexane ring contains 6 C-C bonds. The substituted ring carbon has 1 C-O bond to the OH oxygen and 1 C-C bond to the side-chain carbon. The side-chain carbon has 1 C-N bond. The two nitrogens are connected by 1 N=N double-bond entity. The second nitrogen has 1 N-O bond to the OH2 oxygen. Total = 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a heavy-atom graph. Assign heavy-atom degrees from the drawing: the substituted ring carbon connects to two ring carbons, the OH oxygen, and the side-chain carbon, degree 4; the other five ring carbons each have two ring neighbors, total degree 10; the side-chain carbon connects to the ring carbon and first nitrogen, degree 2; the OH oxygen attached to the ring has degree 1; the first nitrogen connects to the side-chain carbon and the second nitrogen, degree 2; the second nitrogen connects to the first nitrogen and the OH2 oxygen, degree 2; the OH2 oxygen has degree 1. The degree sum is 4 + 10 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 22, so the number of unique non-H bonds is 22/2 = 11.
